content: {"summary":"The CPU increase was modest and not the root cause; the Hikari pool was fully occupied by the month‑end reconciliation batch, leading to pending connections and 503 errors. The incident was resolved by lowering the batch parallelism and the team explicitly chose not to raise maximumPoolSize, recommending throttling the batch instead of changing the pool size mid‑incident.","likely_cause":"Reconciliation batch parallelism exceeding the Hikari pool size, causing connection exhaustion","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"CPU elevation was not the primary cause; connection exhaustion drove the outage.","evidence_ids":["RB-013#2"],"quote":"CPU on that pod was clearly elevated, around two thirds of its limit."},{"text":"All pool connections were held by reconciliation workers, causing pending requests.","evidence_ids":["RB-013#3"],"quote":"Every one of the 20 connections was held by a thread named `recon-worker-*`."},{"text":"Operators resolved without increasing maximumPoolSize and advise against bumping it mid‑incident.","evidence_ids":["RB-013#6"],"quote":"We did not raise `maximumPoolSize`."},{"text":"Do not touch the pool; throttle the batch instead.","evidence_ids":["RB-013#7"],"quote":"If it's the batch, throttle the batch; don't touch the pool."}],"next_checks":["Check current LEDGER_RECON_PARALLELISM setting","Monitor hikaricp_connections_pending versus CPU usage","Verify maximumPoolSize has not been changed during the incident","Consider configuring a separate connection pool for batch jobs"]}
